<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. VIII.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|161}}</noinclude>them: for they vvere taken vvith great feare. And he going vp into the boate, returned. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=38}}† And the man out of vvhom the deuils vvere departed, desired him that he might be vvith him. But {{sc|Iesvs}} dimissed him, saying, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=39}}† Returne into thy house, and tel hovv great things God hath done to thee. And he vvent through the vvhole citie, preaching hovv great things {{sc|Iesvs}} had done to him.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=40}}† And it came to passe: vvhen {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas returned, the multitude receiued him. and al vvere expecting him. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=41}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 9, 18. Mar. 5, 22.''}}* behold there came a man vvhose name vvas Iairus, and he vvas Prince of the Synagogue: and he fel at the feete of {{sc|Iesvs}}, desiring him that he vvould enter into his house, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=42}}† because he had an only daughter almost tvvelue yeres old, and she vvas a dying. And it chaunced, vvhiles he vvent, he vvas thronged of the multitudes.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=43}}† And there vvas {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ See the Annotations vpon S. Matthew ''c. 9, 19''.}}∷ a certaine vvoman in a fluxe of bloud from tvvelue yeres past, vvhich had bestovved al her substance vpon Physicions, neither could she be cured of any: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=44}}† she came behind him, and touched the hemme of his garment: and forthvvith the fluxe of her bloud stinted, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=45}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said, VVho is it that touched me? And al denying, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ It is an euident signe of prerogatiue, that Peter only is named so often as cheefe of the company. ''Mar. 1, 36. Act. 5, 29. Luc. 9, 32. Mar. 16, 7. 1 Cor. 15, 5''.}}∷ Peter said, and they that vvere vvith him, Maister, the multitudes throng and presse thee, and doest thou say, VVho touched me? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=46}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said, Some bodie hath touched me. for I know that there is vertue proceded from me. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=47}}† And the vvoman seeing, that she vvas not hid, came trembling, and fel dovvne before his feete: and for vvhat cause she had touched him, she shevved before al the people: and hovv forthvvith she vvas made vvhole. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=48}}† But he said to her, Daughter, thy faith hath made the safe, goe thy vvay in peace.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=49}}† As he vvas yet speaking, there commeth one to the Prince of the synagogue, saying to him, That thy daughter is dead, trouble him not. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=50}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} hearing this vvord, ansvvered the father of the maide, Feare not: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ See the Annotations vpon S. Marke ''c. 5, 36''.}}∷ beleeue only, and she shal be safe. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=51}}† And vvhen he vvas come to the house, he permitted not any man to enter in vvith him, but Peter, and Iames, and Iohn, and the father and mother of the maide. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=52}}† And al vvept, and mourned for her. But he said, VVeepe not, the maide is not dead, but sleepeth. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=53}}† And they derided him, knovving that she vvas dead. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=54}}† But he holding her hand cried saying, Maide arise. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=55}}† And {{sup|‖}} her spirit returned, and she rose<noinclude>{{rh||X|incontinent.}}</noinclude>
